title: Fix dogfood papercuts: env var naming consistency, README clarity, and better errors
author: Sabrina James
body: Context: Dogfooding surfaced a few recurring papercuts that show up in Support too: (1) env var names drifted across templates/languages, (2) the top-level README didn’t make the "fast path" obvious, and (3) error messages were missing actionable hints (especially around 429/backoff, missing keys, and vector DB connectivity). This PR standardizes config names, improves READMEs, and tightens error messages while keeping backwards compatibility for a short deprecation window. Changes: Env var contract alignment: canonical keys are now REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_BASE_URL, REDWOOD_MODEL, REDWOOD_TENANT_ID, REDWOOD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS, REDWOOD_MAX_RETRIES, and REDWOOD_RETRY_MAX_SLEEP_MS. Added a small compatibility layer that accepts legacy aliases (e.g., REDWOOD_KEY, API_KEY, REDWOOD_TIMEOUT) and logs a single deprecation warning at startup with the new key name; removed a few template-local one-offs that were never documented. Updated .env.example files across Python + TypeScript templates to match, and updated docs snippets to reference canonical keys only. README improvements: reworked the root README to make "run locally in <15 min" the first section; clarified the three template entry points (rag, agents, rag+agents) and added a consistent "Troubleshooting" section (429s, streaming disconnects, timeouts on large docs, CORS when running behind a proxy). Added explicit notes on request_id/traceparent propagation and how to find the trace in Console when something fails. Error message improvements: standardized a small set of human-readable error messages and exit codes for startup/config errors (missing API key, invalid base URL, invalid model), and improved runtime errors to include request_id + a stable error_class and a short remediation hint (e.g., "429: backoff + check quota" / "vector store unreachable: check compose health" / "timeout: raise REDWOOD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS for large ingests"). The goal is to reduce "works on my machine" loops and cut down Support pings. Notes: This is intended to be non-breaking for existing users because we still accept legacy env vars for now; follow-up will remove aliases after the 2026-03 template tag and docs deprecation period. Testing: ran template smoke tests locally for python-rag (ingest + query), ts-rag (streaming), and agents (tool calling stub) and validated that traces include request.id and tenant.id, and that startup prints the expected deprecation warning once. Release notes: none (template-only), but this is a quality-of-life improvement ahead of the docs-site push.
commits: config: introduce canonical env var map + legacy alias support (single warning)
docs: rewrite root README quickstart + troubleshooting matrix
templates(py): normalize env var names + improve startup validation errors
templates(ts): normalize env var names + improve 429/timeout error messaging
chore: update .env.example files and snippet checks
review_conversation: Monica Patel: Can we make sure the alias warning is printed once per process and not once per request? Also please confirm the 429 error path still includes retry-after if present.

Sabrina James: Good call. Alias warnings are now gated behind a module-level once() helper (prints once on startup). For 429, we preserve Retry-After when provided and include it in the error message + logs as retry_after_ms.
Wei Chen: README is much better. Two nits: (1) put the env var table before the "Optional" section, and (2) call out the exact header name for request id propagation (we echo x-redwood-request-id).
Sabrina James: Updated. Env var table moved up; request id propagation section now explicitly references x-redwood-request-id + traceparent passthrough and points to Console trace lookup.
Sean Gallagher: On timeouts: the remediation should mention increasing timeout specifically for ingestion vs query. Otherwise folks will crank timeouts everywhere.

Sabrina James: Agreed. Split hint: ingestion timeout guidance references the ingest worker and suggests raising REDWOOD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS for ingestion only (we already support per-component config in python); query path keeps a smaller default and suggests chunking before raising.
Marcus Lin: Security: ensure we don’t print full env var values in the new config validation errors (especially API key). Also make sure .env.example doesn’t encourage committing secrets.
Sabrina James: Confirmed: errors only print which variable is missing/invalid; never the value. Also added a line to each README and .env.example header: "Do not commit .env; rotate keys if exposed".
Dana Lo: TS template: please keep naming consistent with the SDK helper (timeout_ms vs timeout). Also ensure the thrown error includes error_class for the telemetry contract.

Sabrina James: Updated TS config naming to timeout_ms internally but exposed env var remains REDWOOD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS. Added error_class to all thrown errors (rate_limit, timeout, config, upstream) and verified metrics tagging in the smoke test logs.
Monica Patel: Looks good after latest push. Approving.
Wei Chen: Approving (thanks for fixing the snippet drift too).
